awards.name: MVP Award
awards.description: Given to the player who earned the most tournament points after playing in at least two eligible rounds.
awards.rule: Requires appearances in at least two eligible tournament rounds. Most points; ties: the player on the confirmed tournament-winning team, then more points per race, then fewer starts. Organizer clarification, September 16, 2026: Essential takes the 27-point MVP tie over wata because Dominance won the tournament.

awards.rule: Requires appearances in at least two eligible tournament rounds. Ties: fewer points per race, then more starts.

awards.name: Nakayama Festa Award
awards.description: Given to the player who won the most points relative to the stats they fielded.
awards.rule: Highest points per 1,000 fielded base stats. Tie: lower total stats.

awards.name: The Flyingsparks Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose opponent-debuff skills activated the most times across their races.
awards.rule: Count each recorded opponent-debuff skill activation across eligible races, up to the runner’s finish. Repeated activations count each time; equipped skills that never activate do not count. Self costs and negative personal traits are excluded. Equal activation totals require a sourced organizer decision.

awards.name: The 5 Nitro Incident Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas late-started the most. The 12-billion-yen incident, now on a five-Nitro budget.
awards.rule: Recorded start delay ≥ 66 ms. Ties: total delay on late starts, then worst start delay.

awards.name: Double Jet Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas entered Rushed mode the most times.
awards.rule: A continuous nonzero Rushed mode is one incident, including mode changes. Tie: total observed Rushed time.

awards.name: Retired Bourbon Award
awards.description: Given to the player with the most verified failed wit checks across all races. Unmet skill conditions do not count.
awards.rule: Only verified failed_wit outcomes. Failed conditions and unresolved outcomes are excluded. Tie: failure rate among verified wit rolls.

awards.name: Asslicker Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas were blocked the most times.
awards.rule: Count unblocked → blocked transitions on the affected runner. Changing blocker without a free interval stays one incident. Tie: total blocked time.

awards.name: Agnes Digital Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas spent the longest total time being blocked.
awards.rule: Sum observed blocked intervals on the affected runner, clipped to their finish. Tie: incident count.

awards.name: The Neck and Neck Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas spent the most estimated total time dueling.
awards.rule: Sum Hakuraku-estimated duel intervals across each player’s runners and races. Uses start events, HP, opponent gaps, skill-adjusted speed, hills and finish time. Sourced verified observations override estimates.

awards.name: Swing for the Fences Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas lost the most estimated distance to lane changes and wider cornering (WT).
awards.rule: Sum estimated WT loss: max(0, min(previous speed, current speed) × frame duration − forward progress), interpolated at each runner’s finish. Includes lane changes and wider cornering. Sourced verified observations override estimates.

awards.name: No More Goo Goo Babies Award
awards.description: Given to the player whose Umas finished the most races at 0 HP.
awards.rule: Count each eligible runner finishing a verified race at exactly 0 HP, once per runner per race. HP is interpolated at that runner’s finish from recorded frames, before display rounding. Hitting 0 earlier or after finishing does not count. Equal totals remain tied.
awards.reason: The metric and all published tiebreakers are tied. One organizer decision is required.
